title: Groups of Multiplicative Type and Arithmetic Tori

items.title: Coordinate Hopf algebras for multiplicative type
items.statement: For an affine k-group scheme G its coordinate algebra carries comultiplication, counit and antipode making it a commutative Hopf k-algebra; Hopf maps respect all three maps, and a group-like element satisfies Δ(a)=a⊗a and ε(a)=1. The group-scheme convention includes nonreduced schemes.

items.title: The affine Hopf dictionary used for multiplicative type
items.statement: Affine k-group schemes are contravariantly equivalent to commutative Hopf k-algebras; a group character G→G_m corresponds exactly to a group-like element of the coordinate algebra, and these correspondences commute with field extension.

items.title: Diagonalizable groups and their character modules
items.statement: For an abelian group M, D_k(M)=Spec k[M] is the affine group with Δ(e_m)=e_m⊗e_m, ε(e_m)=1, S(e_m)=e_{-m}; over a base S, D_S(M) is glued from the charts Spec R[M], and a diagonalizable group is one isomorphic to some D_S(M). Its character group is X(G)=Hom(G,G_m), and D_k(M)(R)=Hom(M,R^×) for every k-algebra R.

items.title: Split diagonalizable groups are dual to abelian groups
items.statement: For every field k, X(D_k(M))=M and Hom(D_k(M),D_k(N))=Hom(N,M) naturally; k[M] is finitely generated as an algebra iff M is finitely generated; and D_k(Z^r⊕⊕_i Z/n_i)≅G_m^r×∏_i μ_{n_i} with μ_n=Spec k[t]/(t^n-1).

items.title: Groups of multiplicative type and tori
items.statement: A finite-type group scheme over a field k is of multiplicative type if it is fpqc locally diagonalizable, and a torus if it is fpqc locally isomorphic to a power of G_m; split means the isomorphism already exists over k. The definition imposes no affineness or separable splitting and includes the trivial torus and nonsmooth groups.

items.title: Affineness of a field form of a diagonalizable group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. If a finite-type k-group scheme G has G_K affine for some field extension K/k, then G is affine. Hence a finite-type group scheme fpqc locally diagonalizable over k is affine and becomes diagonalizable over a field extension, so the full finite-type formulation of multiplicative type and the affine formulation give the same class.

items.title: Finite coalgebra pieces of a multiplicative coordinate algebra
items.statement: Every finite subset of a coalgebra over a field lies in a finite-dimensional subcoalgebra C. If A is a Hopf algebra with A⊗_k K≅K[M] as Hopf algebras for an extension field K, then the dual algebra C* of every such C becomes a product of copies of K after extension to K.

items.title: Multiplicative type groups split over a finite Galois extension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For an arbitrary field k with separable closure k_s, every finite-type group of multiplicative type over k is diagonalizable over k_s and over a finite Galois subextension L/k of k_s/k.

items.title: Finite Galois descent for the Hopf algebras of multiplicative type
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension L/k with group Γ, a commutative Hopf L-algebra B with semilinear Γ-action preserving the Hopf maps descends to the Hopf k-algebra A=B^Γ with L⊗_k A≅B; if B is finitely generated then so is A, equivariant Hopf maps descend uniquely, and the fixed algebra of a canonical scalar extension L⊗A_0 is A_0.

items.title: Continuous Galois character modules
items.statement: Fix a separable closure k_s/k and Γ_k=Gal(k_s/k) with its Krull topology. A continuous Galois character module is a finitely generated abelian group with a Γ_k-action continuous for the discrete topology, equivalently with open stabilizers; X^*(G)=Hom_{k_s}(G_{k_s},G_{m,k_s}) carries the transport action, and AC is declared because the separable splitting lemma supplies finiteness for nonsmooth G.

items.title: Multiplicative type groups and Galois character modules
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Over an arbitrary field k, G↦X^*(G) is a contravariant equivalence between finite-type k-group schemes of multiplicative type and finitely generated abelian groups with continuous Γ_k-action, with quasi-inverse M↦Spec((k_s[M])^{Γ_k}) for the action σ(c e_m)=σ(c)e_{σm}. No smoothness, connectedness, perfection or characteristic-zero hypothesis is required.

items.title: Tori correspond exactly to torsion-free character lattices
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A finite-type group of multiplicative type over any field is a torus iff its character module is torsion-free, equivalently free of finite rank; the classification restricts to an anti-equivalence between k-tori and free finite-rank abelian groups with continuous Galois action, and nonzero torsion in the character module excludes a torus even when the group is smooth.

title: Groups of Multiplicative Type and Arithmetic Tori — Examples

items.title: The character lattice of a split torus
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every field k, T=G_m^r has X^*(T)=Z^r with trivial Galois action; a vector (n_1,…,n_r) represents the character (t_1,…,t_r)↦∏ t_i^{n_i}, and a map G_m^r→G_m^s is an integer s×r matrix, in every characteristic.

items.strategy: Read off the monomial characters from the split dictionary and count maps by basis images, including rank zero and trivial source or target.

items.title: A quadratic norm-one torus and its sign action
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, char k≠2 and d∈k^× a nonsquare. T=Spec k[x,y]/(x²−dy²−1) with (x,y)(x',y')=(xx'+dyy',xy'+yx') is a nonsplit torus with character module Z on which the nontrivial automorphism of k(√d)/k acts by n↦−n; for k=R and d=−1 this is the circle group x²+y²=1.

items.strategy: Identify T with norm-one elements of k(√d), split over L=k(√d) with t↦t^{-1}, and use the classification to read the sign action and rule out splitting.

items.title: The multiplicative group scheme μ_p is not a smooth torus
items.statement: Over a field k of characteristic p>0, μ_p=Spec k[t]/(t^p−1) is of multiplicative type with X^*(μ_p)=Z/p, but it is not a torus because the character module has torsion, and it is not smooth: its local ring k[u]/(u^p) has embedding dimension one and Krull dimension zero. This refutes 'every finite-type group of multiplicative type over a field is a smooth torus'.
